# Contributing to Kition SDK

Real document editors in your app, and the same documents for your AI agents.

Thank you for contributing; every change keeps the checks green.

## Scope

| Path | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/` | The Rust crates: the `KitDocument` contract, the Kit Data Model, the headless host, and `kition-kits` |
| `packages/` | The npm packages under the `@kition` scope |
| `docs/` | The SDK guide (`docs/sdk/`), the platform contracts (`docs/platform/`), and the development and quality references |
| `examples/` | The grid example kit, the embed app, scripts, and the agent example |
| `schemas/` | JSON Schemas: the kit manifest, the Kit Process Protocol, the kits service, the MCP tools |
| `tools/` | The repository's checks and generators, and the container image (`tools/container/`) |
| `templates/` | The quality and community files that `tools/sync-quality.mjs` and `tools/sync-community.mjs` write into Kition repositories |
| `features.yaml`, `cases/` | The feature catalogue and its cases ([docs/quality.md](../docs/quality.md)) |

## Local setup

Use Rust 1.95 or later with rustfmt, clippy, and the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target, wasm-pack 0.13.1, Node.js 22.23.4 or a later 22.x release, and pnpm 10.34.9.

```sh
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
cargo build -p kition-kit-mock   # host tests launch the mock kit's executable
cargo test
pnpm typecheck
pnpm test
```

The workspace links Kition Tessera, so clone [kition-tessera](https://github.com/KitionAI/kition-tessera) beside this repository before `pnpm install`. [docs/development.md](../docs/development.md) covers building and packing the npm packages.

Before you open a pull request, run the check; it must exit 0:

```sh
pnpm -s typecheck && pnpm -s test && cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
```

The full checks and tests run on GitHub, in the repository's CI run (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`),
for your pull request too; it must pass before the pull request merges.

## Rules

The full rules are in [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md), and [docs/quality.md](../docs/quality.md) is the
testing reference; they apply to people and to coding agents alike. The ones that most often
matter:

- **Tests are the spec.** The feature catalogue (`features.yaml`) and each case's `intent` say how
  this repository must behave. A new feature adds an entry to `features.yaml` and at least one
  gating test; a bug fix starts with a failing case under `cases/regressions/issue-<n>/`.
- **Expected results are protected.** Never change files under `cases/**/expected/`, or the
  `expected`, `tolerance`, `reference`, `input` or `steps` of an existing case, to make a test
  pass, and never weaken a test. Only a maintainer approves an expected-result change.
- **No compatibility layers**: no aliases, old names, old file suffixes, migrations, or readers
  for old formats.
- **English** for code, comments, docs, and commit messages.

## Pull requests

1. Open an issue first for a new feature or a change to a public interface, so the shape is agreed before the work.
2. Keep a pull request to one change. Add or update a case or test with it.
3. Run the check above; it must exit 0. Add an entry to `CHANGELOG.md` under
   **Unreleased**.
4. For a visual change, add screenshots.
